First, we write down the standard matrix of $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14152450/assets/94a5bcbcf9377b4cc2047b1cbab522eec499bcc5f438f6ee97e2e16e7f837b42.svg)

Recall that $\textrm{nullity}(\mathbf{T}) = \textrm{nullity}(T) = \textrm{dim}(\textrm{Null}(T)).$

In order to find $\textrm{dim}(\textrm{Null}(T)),$ we reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 10 & -1 \\ -6 & -12 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -6 & -12 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has no non-pivot columns. Therefore, 

$$
\textrm{nullity}(\mathbf{T})=\textrm{dim}(\textrm{Null}(T))=0.
$$
